A collapse of their currencies could push Japanese bond yields higher and force arbitrage unwindings, which would then spread to US Treasuries and equities.

Thus, the US aims to reduce three major risks: preventing a sharp yen drop that would spike Japanese bond yields, containing financial stress from spilling across Asia, and averting disorderly capital flows that could hit US bonds. Since the start of the year, semiconductor ETFs have attracted about $53 billion, the semiconductor index has pulled back in the short term, but the logic of AI‑driven capital spending remains intact, and Washington does not want its allies’ assets to be harvested by short‑sellers at the end of the leverage cycle.

However, intervention does not equal a trend reversal. Rate checks can scare off speculators, but if the US‑Japan interest‑rate differential remains unaddressed and Korean equity deleveraging is not resolved, the yen and won could still be tested again.

The market consensus is that this round of coordination first contains "disorderly depreciation," buying time for South Korean regulators to implement August measures and for the Bank of Japan to assess rates next month. True pricing power will return based on semiconductor earnings, corporate buybacks and global AI spending.

The US’s direct involvement – a first in 30 years – carries a signal that outweighs the monetary amount itself. Washington is now treating the stability of Japanese and Korean exchange rates and assets as an integral part of its domestic financial defence line.

items.title: 傳波灣國家對美缺乏針對伊朗戰略很不滿  「這一國」希望華府硬幹
items.title_en: Gulf Nations Growingly Dissatisfied with U.S. Lack of Strategy Against Iran, One Country Wants Washington to Act Firmly
paras: 《華爾街日報》週日 (2 日) 引述知情人士報導，隨著美伊戰事延燒、領土頻遭伊朗襲擊，波斯灣國家對美國遲未拿出針對伊朗的整體戰略愈發不滿。
報導指出，近幾週以來，美國在波斯灣的盟友持續要求華府增供防空攔截器，並應明確承諾在針鋒相對衝突延續下，美軍將實質保護其領空與設施。
波斯灣陣營對降溫態度分歧。多數國家憂被拖入消耗戰，盼美方壓制局勢，阿拉伯聯合大公國等則反向操作，近日主動接觸美國總統川普，說服其對伊朗採更強硬措施，包括擴大威懾與打擊選項。
報導還說，一位伊朗外交官表示，該國官員已看清川普國內政治弱點，必要時或加以利用，若外交管道破裂，革命衛隊正評估「先發制人打擊」方案，不等對手出手再報復。
報導凸顯美式安全承諾的張力，波斯灣付費換保護，卻陷「被拖下水」與「傘漏雨」兩難；華府既要穩住盟友、又要控成本與避大戰。
短期內，變數在於美方能否補足攔截彈庫、給出駐軍保證，以及阿聯的強硬遊說會否把川普推回極限施壓老路；德黑蘭則在外交與軍事邊界試探，讓中東危機管理更脆弱。
paras_en: The Wall Street Journal reported on Sunday (the 2nd) that, as the U.S.-Iran conflict drags on and Iranian attacks on territory become frequent, Gulf states are increasingly unhappy with the United States for not presenting a comprehensive strategy against Iran.

The report notes that in recent weeks, U.S. allies in the Gulf have repeatedly asked Washington to increase the supply of air‑defense interceptors and to make a clear commitment that, should the confrontation continue, the U.S. military will concretely protect their airspace and facilities.

The Gulf camp is divided over how to cool the situation. Most countries fear being drawn into a war of attrition and hope the U.S. will curb the escalation, while the United Arab Emirates and others are taking the opposite approach, recently reaching out to President Trump to persuade him to adopt tougher measures against Iran, including expanding deterrence and strike options.

The article also says an Iranian diplomat stated that Iranian officials have identified weaknesses in Trump’s domestic politics and may exploit them if necessary; if diplomatic channels break down, the Revolutionary Guard is assessing a "pre‑emptive strike" plan, waiting to retaliate only after the opponent acts.

The report highlights the tension in the U.S. security guarantee: Gulf states pay for protection but find themselves caught between being "dragged into the water" and having a "leaky umbrella"; Washington must both reassure its allies and control costs while avoiding a major war.

In the short term, the variables hinge on whether the U.S. can replenish interceptor stockpiles, provide troop‑deployment guarantees, and whether the UAE’s hard‑line lobbying will push Trump back toward extreme pressure tactics; Tehran, meanwhile, is probing diplomatic and military boundaries, making Middle‑East crisis management even more fragile.

items.title: AI記憶體行情迎「抄底機會」？《巴隆》：7月修正後估值浮現吸引力
items.title_en: AI Memory Stocks Offer a ‘Bottom‑Fishing Opportunity’? Barron's: Post‑July Corrections Reveal Attractive Valuations
paras: 過去一年狂飆不止的記憶體概念股，在七月吃了一記悶棍。市場人士認為，這波急速回檔反而讓過熱的評價回到較合理水位，對打算進場的投資人來說未必是壞事。
根據《巴隆周刊》報導，美系記憶體大廠中， SanDisk (SNDKV-US) 七月股價重挫 47%，創下 2025 年 2 月從威騰電子 (WDC-US) 分拆掛牌以來單月最差表現；美光科技 (MU-US) 同期下跌 29%，寫下 2015 年以來最慘的一個月。
韓系對手同樣難以倖免。SK 海力士 (KR000660) 與三星電子 (KR005930) 七月分別下滑 35% 與 21%。
追蹤動態隨機存取記憶體（DRAM）產業的 Roundhill DRAM ETF(DRAM-US) 當月跌幅達 32%，來到五月中旬以來新低。
分析指出，不論是在南韓與美國市場，這波修正背後，不乏投機炒作破功的戲碼。但正因如此，分析師認為記憶體類股的評價已重新洗牌，對新資金而言吸引力反而提升。
回顧過去一年，在供給吃緊與人工智慧（AI）需求爆發雙重帶動下，記憶體股價一度飆出三位數漲幅，價格屢創歷史新高。以美光為例，其六月公布的財報顯示單季獲利較前一季翻倍，營業利益率高達 81%。
然而，也因為如此，在記憶體股撐起大盤半邊天的南韓，不少散戶借貸重壓 AI 題材，助長了股價的劇烈波動。
報導指出，美國市場雖無同等程度的集中風險，但這股投機熱潮仍可能跨海蔓延。尤其 SK 海力士 (SKHY-US) 已於 7 月 10 日在那斯達克掛牌，更是讓這種投機行為雪上加霜。
Empower Investments 首席投資策略師 Marta Norton 表示，記憶體股近來的氛圍「有點像加密貨幣」，暗指不論外界如何評價虛擬貨幣，其高波動性總能吸引想快速獲利的投機客。
耐人尋味的是，就在 Norton 發表上述看法後沒幾分鐘，《華爾街日報》隨即報導，避險基金 Situational Awareness 在蒙受重大虧損後，已將手中大部分部位出售給避險基金 Citadel，而 Sandisk 正是 Situational Awareness 原先最大的持股部位。
《巴隆》警告，想投資記憶體股，恐怕仍得先做好承受劇烈震盪的心理準備。過去三個月，Roundhill DRAM ETF 的貝塔係數（衡量股價相對大盤波動程度的常用指標）高達 5.2，代表其波動幅度約為大盤的五倍。
不過，報導也指出，若能忍受高波動，八月或許是相對划算的進場時機。目前 DRAM ETF 的股價僅為未來 12 個月預估獲利的 4.8 倍，遠低於六月底一度超過 10 倍的高點。
多項跡象顯示，這波由 AI 需求驅動的記憶體景氣循環仍處於上升軌道。SK 海力士本週稍早公布的第二季財報雖不如分析師預期，但營業利益仍較去年同期大增 257%。
儘管市場預期隨著新產能陸續開出，供給增加終將壓縮利潤空間，但就目前而言，記憶體供應商仍握有議價優勢，紛紛與客戶簽訂長期供貨協議。
Norton 指出，目前並無跡象顯示 AI 相關需求會「一夜之間消失」。
市場接下來將聚焦 8 月 5 日，Sandisk 屆時將公布第四財季財報，這將是檢驗整體產業需求力道的下一個重要指標。華爾街預估，該公司營收與平均售價將較去年同期成長逾四倍。
paras_en: After a year of relentless gains, memory‑chip stocks took a sharp hit in July. Market participants say the rapid pull‑back has brought overheated valuations back to more reasonable levels, which may not be a bad thing for investors looking to enter.

According to Barron's, among the major U.S. memory makers, SanDisk (SNDKV‑US) saw its share price plunge 47% in July, marking the worst single‑month performance since its spin‑off from Western Digital (WDC‑US) in February 2025; Micron Technology (MU‑US) fell 29% over the same period, its steepest month since 2015.
South Korean rivals were similarly hard hit. SK Hynix (KR000660) and Samsung Electronics (KR005930) slid 35% and 21% respectively in July.
The Roundhill DRAM ETF (DRAM‑US), which tracks the dynamic random‑access memory (DRAM) sector, dropped 32% for the month, hitting a new low not seen since mid‑May.

Analysts note that, whether in South Korea or the United States, the correction reflects a bust of speculative froth. As a result, they argue that memory‑chip valuations have been reshuffled, making the sector more appealing to fresh capital.

Looking back over the past year, tight supply and a surge in AI demand drove memory stocks up triple‑digit percentages, repeatedly setting all‑time highs. For example, Micron’s June earnings report showed quarterly profit doubling versus the prior quarter, with an operating margin of 81%.
However, that same rally helped South Korean markets, where retail investors leveraged heavily on AI‑related themes, amplifying price volatility.

The report adds that, while the U.S. market lacks the same concentration risk, the speculative fervor could spill over overseas. The situation was exacerbated when SK Hynix (SKHY‑US) listed on Nasdaq on July 10, adding fuel to the speculative fire.

Marta Norton, chief investment strategist at Empower Investments, likened the current mood around memory stocks to “cryptocurrency,” implying that regardless of how virtual currencies are judged, their high volatility always draws profit‑hungry speculators.

Intriguingly, minutes after Norton’s comments, the Wall Street Journal reported that hedge fund Situational Awareness, after suffering heavy losses, sold most of its positions to hedge fund Citadel, and SanDisk had been its largest holding.

Barron's warns that investors in memory stocks must be prepared for severe swings. Over the past three months, the Roundhill DRAM ETF’s beta—a common measure of a stock’s volatility relative to the market—has been as high as 5.2, meaning its price moves about five times the broader market’s moves.

Nevertheless, the article points out that for those who can tolerate the volatility, August could be a relatively cheap entry point. The DRAM ETF is currently trading at 4.8 times forward 12‑month earnings, well below the peak of over 10 times seen at the end of June.

Multiple signs suggest the AI‑driven memory cycle is still on an upward trajectory. SK Hynix’s early‑quarter Q2 earnings this week missed analyst forecasts but still posted operating profit up 257% year‑over‑year.
Although the market expects new capacity to gradually increase supply and compress margins, memory suppliers still enjoy pricing power and are signing long‑term supply contracts with customers.
Norton notes there is no indication that AI‑related demand will “disappear overnight.”

All eyes will turn to SanDisk’s fourth‑quarter earnings release on August 5, which will be the next key gauge of overall industry demand. Wall Street estimates the company’s revenue and average selling price will grow more than four‑fold versus the same period last year.

items.title: 輝達市值有望達到10兆美元？外媒點出「下一波成長引擎」
items.title_en: NVIDIA’s Market Cap Could Reach $10 Trillion? Foreign Media Spot the “Next Growth Engine”
paras: 又一場由晶片大廠輝達 (NVDA-US) 主導的技術革命正加速成形，並有望成為支撐其股價長期表現的重要成長引擎。這場革命涵蓋自動駕駛與機器人市場，即輝達執行長黃仁勳口中的「物理 AI」（Physical AI）。
根據《The Motley Fool》報導，在 ChatGPT 掀起生成式 AI 浪潮之前，輝達市值僅約 3,860 億美元；如今受惠於這波 AI 熱潮，公司市值已翻漲逾十倍，逼近 5 兆美元大關。
而現在，包括自駕車與機器人技術的「物理 AI」，正被視為公司未來成長的另一股重要動能。
輝達最廣為人知的是其 GPU，以及支援資料中心 AI 運算的相關硬體，但該公司在物理 AI 領域的核心元件方面，同樣建立了顯著的競爭優勢。
以 Jetson Thor 超級電腦為例，它被市場普遍視為 AI 推論與機器人模擬領域的領導產品。輝達將 Jetson Thor 提供給眾多機器人公司，包括波士頓動力、亞馬遜 (AMZN-US) Robotics、卡特彼勒 (CAT-US) 、迪爾 (DE-US) 等。
這些企業利用 Jetson Thor 執行電腦視覺等應用，協助機器人與各類設備運作，例如支援亞馬遜倉庫中的自動化作業，或協助迪爾在農業場域操作智慧農機。
除了機器人企業外，Jetson Thor 也已獲得 Meta(META-US) 、OpenAI 等科技公司，以及醫療科技公司美敦力公司 (MDT-US) 採用。
儘管機器人市場正快速成長，但對輝達而言，更大的商機似乎來自自動駕駛汽車市場。而外媒指出，該產業可能正邁向關鍵轉折點。
例如，Alphabet(GOOGL-US) 旗下 Waymo 目前每週已提供 50 萬趟付費自動駕駛叫車服務，較一年前增加逾一倍，服務範圍涵蓋 10 個都會區。特斯拉 (TSLA-US) 的 Robotaxi 服務也已擴展至 7 座城市，其他自動駕駛公司同樣持續加快布局。
雖然 Waymo 與特斯拉並非輝達在自動駕駛領域的直接合作夥伴，但其已攜手多家重要業者，包括 Uber (UBER-US) 、Toyota、Stellantis (FCAU-US) 、賓士，以及中國兩大電動車製造商比亞迪 (002594-CN) 和吉利汽車 (00175-HK) 。
其中，輝達在汽車領域最重要的合作夥伴是 Uber。這家叫車平台正與輝達及 Stellantis 等原始設備製造商合作，計畫部署至少 5,000 輛 L4 自動駕駛車輛，打造 Robotaxi 車隊。
輝達的 DRIVE AGX Hyperion 自動駕駛平台將作為這些自動駕駛車輛的運算核心，並同樣為上述其他合作夥伴提供自動駕駛運算能力。
報導指出，輝達的汽車業務目前規模仍然不大，2026 會計年度營收為 23 億美元，較前一年度成長 39%。
不過，自 2027 會計年度起，輝達調整了財務報告架構，將原本三個非資料中心業務部門，包括遊戲與 AI PC、專業視覺化以及汽車與機器人，整併為全新的邊緣運算事業群。
因此，投資人將無法再像過去一樣，清楚掌握汽車業務的獨立財務表現，但輝達仍持續對外更新相關業務進展。
分析指出，儘管目前規模仍小，但物理 AI 業務可望在更長期的時間內創造可觀回報。
執行長黃仁勳近日救表示，該業務目前的年化營收已達 100 億美元，並預估未來十年內可望成長至 1,000 億美元。

為何它可能讓輝達市值衝上 10 兆美元？

輝達目前市值已達 5 兆美元，但其預估本益比僅 22 倍，甚至低於標普 500 指數的平均水準，儘管華爾街分析師預估，公司今年營收仍將成長 82%。
這種估值與成長表現不相稱的現象，主要反映市場對半導體產業景氣循環的疑慮，以及 AI 泡沫風險的擔憂，因為投資人正押注，輝達目前創紀錄的獲利終將回落，至少成長速度將大幅放緩。
好消息是，物理 AI 業務正好為輝達提供了一項重要的支撐。
報導稱，基於這是一條獨立於資料中心及生成式 AI 的業務主軸，且由於交通運輸屬於長期且持續存在的需求，其景氣循環波動預料將較小。
此外，輝達在自動駕駛業務中，包括 Drive AV 軟體平台在內的部分產品，採用軟體即服務（SaaS）的訂閱模式。
由於軟體公司的估值通常高於硬體公司，外媒認為，輝達物理 AI 業務的估值倍數，有機會明顯高於其硬體業務。
如果物理 AI 業務未來達成 1,000 億美元營收目標，依據其成長速度與獲利能力推估，該業務本身的市值就可能達到 2 兆美元甚至更高。
更重要的是，物理 AI 業務有助於降低輝達對生成式 AI 市場景氣的依賴，提升公司整體抗景氣循環能力，進一步帶動整體估值上升。
換句話說，若再結合資料中心核心業務持續擴張，輝達在未來幾年內邁向 10 兆美元市值，並非難以想像。
paras_en: Another chip‑giant‑led technological revolution, this time driven by NVIDIA (NVDA‑US), is accelerating and is expected to become a key long‑term growth engine for its stock. The revolution spans autonomous driving and robotics – what CEO Jensen Huang calls “Physical AI.”

According to The Motley Fool, before the ChatGPT‑sparked generative‑AI wave, NVIDIA’s market value was only about $386 billion. Benefiting from the current AI boom, the company’s valuation has now multiplied more than tenfold, edging toward the $5 trillion mark.
Now, “Physical AI,” which includes self‑driving and robotics technologies, is being seen as another major growth driver for the company’s future.
NVIDIA is best known for its GPUs and hardware that power data‑center AI computing, but it has also built a strong competitive edge in core components for Physical AI.

Take the Jetson Thor supercomputer, widely regarded as the leading product for AI inference and robot simulation. NVIDIA supplies Jetson Thor to many robotics firms, including Boston Dynamics, Amazon (AMZN‑US) Robotics, Caterpillar (CAT‑US) and Deere (DE‑US).

These companies use Jetson Thor for computer‑vision tasks that help robots and various equipment operate – for example, supporting automation in Amazon warehouses or enabling Deere’s smart farm machines.
Beyond robotics firms, Jetson Thor has also been adopted by tech giants such as Meta (META‑US), OpenAI, and medical‑technology company Medtronic (MDT‑US).
While the robotics market is growing fast, the bigger opportunity for NVIDIA appears to be the autonomous‑vehicle sector, which foreign media say may be reaching a pivotal turning point.

For instance, Alphabet’s (GOOGL‑US) Waymo now provides 500,000 paid autonomous‑ride trips per week, more than double a year ago, across ten metropolitan areas. Tesla’s (TSLA‑US) Robotaxi service has also expanded to seven cities, and other self‑driving firms are accelerating their deployments.

Although Waymo and Tesla are not direct NVIDIA partners in autonomous driving, NVIDIA has teamed up with several key players, including Uber (UBER‑US), Toyota, Stellantis (FCAU‑US), Mercedes‑Benz, and China’s two biggest EV makers BYD (002594‑CN) and Geely (00175‑HK).

Among automotive partners, Uber is NVIDIA’s most important collaborator. The ride‑hailing platform is working with NVIDIA and OEMs such as Stellantis to deploy at least 5,000 Level‑4 autonomous vehicles for a Robotaxi fleet.
NVIDIA’s DRIVE AGX Hyperion autonomous‑driving platform will serve as the compute core for those vehicles and will also provide autonomous‑driving compute power to the other partners mentioned above.
The report notes that NVIDIA’s automotive business is still modest, with fiscal‑2026 revenue projected at $2.3 billion, up 39% from the prior year.

Starting fiscal‑2027, NVIDIA will restructure its reporting, folding its three non‑data‑center segments—Gaming & AI PC, Professional Visualization, and Automotive & Robotics—into a new Edge Computing business group.
As a result, investors will no longer be able to see a separate financial picture for the automotive unit, though NVIDIA will continue to update the market on its progress.
Analysts say that although the segment is small today, Physical AI could generate substantial returns over a longer horizon.
CEO Jensen Huang recently said the business now generates about $10 billion in annual revenue and could grow to $100 billion within ten years.
Why could this push NVIDIA’s market cap to $10 trillion?
NVIDIA’s market value is already around $5 trillion, but its forward P/E is only about 22×—below the S&P 500 average—despite Wall Street forecasting an 82% revenue increase this year.
This mismatch reflects concerns about semiconductor cycle volatility and AI‑bubble risk, as investors bet that NVIDIA’s record profits will eventually taper and growth will slow markedly.
The good news is that Physical AI offers a solid counterbalance.
Because it is a business line independent of data‑center and generative AI, and because transportation demand is long‑term and persistent, its cyclical swings are expected to be milder.
Moreover, parts of NVIDIA’s autonomous‑driving portfolio, including the Drive AV software platform, are sold on a software‑as‑a‑service (SaaS) subscription model.

Software companies typically command higher valuation multiples than hardware firms, so foreign media argue that Physical AI could be valued at a significantly higher multiple than NVIDIA’s hardware businesses.
If Physical AI eventually reaches $100 billion in revenue, its own market valuation could climb to $2 trillion or more, based on its growth and profitability profile.
More importantly, the Physical AI segment would reduce NVIDIA’s reliance on the cyclical generative‑AI market, bolstering its overall resilience and lifting its total valuation.
In other words, combined with continued expansion of its core data‑center business, a $10 trillion market cap for NVIDIA in the coming years is not unimaginable.

items.title: 40天驚魂記！從市值崩跌規模超過去年GDP到單日飆18% 韓股去槓桿動盪結束了？
items.title_en: 40-Day Nightmare: From a Market‑Cap Collapse Exceeding Last Year's GDP to an 18% One‑Day Surge—Has the Korean Stock De‑Leverage Turmoil Ended?
paras: 過去 40 天，韓股上演極端劇本，在 6 月 23 日至 7 月 30 日，南韓綜合股指 (KOSPI 跌去近四成，超過 2800 兆韓元市值灰飛煙滅，規模竟超過南韓 2025 年全年 GDP；部分個股兩倍槓桿產品自高點回檔逾 80%。
戲劇性轉折發生在上周五 (7 月 31 日)，KOSPI 單日反彈近 18%，三星電子漲 26.81%、SK 海力士一度觸及 30% 漲停，部分兩倍做多槓桿 ETF 單日飆漲超 60%，創史上最大單日漲幅，但也讓市場更焦慮：這究竟是去槓桿尾聲的死貓跳，還是基本面即將接手定價的前奏？
一切的種子在 5 月埋下，南韓推出追蹤三星電子、SK 海力士單日表現的兩倍槓桿 ETF，上漲時賺錢效應吸金，下跌時為維持固定槓桿倍數必須機械減倉，疊加融資盤平倉，把市場推入負向循環。
根據韓國金融投資協會數據，自 5 月初至 7 月 29 日，券商對未結算款項的強制賣出累計約 2.6 兆韓元。
根據高盛上周六 (1 日) 數據，截至上周五，南韓槓桿 ETF 資產規模從峰值 530 億美元降至 240 億美元，槓桿部位佔自由流通股比重降至 1.9%；但過去一、兩周資金外流後，散戶再度加碼，潛在每日再平衡資金流雖較峰值減半，「影響依然顯著」。
華泰證券表示，韓股去槓桿進入「最後一哩路」，但尾端風險未消：其一，槓桿 ETF 部位仍偏高，美國英偉達、特斯拉相關產品佔流通市值約 0.4%，南韓明顯過頭；其二，規模縮水主要靠標的跌價而非贖回，二級市場買盤未冷；其三，KOSPI 200 波動率指數 (VKOSPI) 上周四處於 2005 年以來 99.6% 分位。
根據華泰估算，槓桿 ETF 佔三星、海力士 30 日均成交比重仍達 11.4%，是高波動核心來源，8 月中政策落地前市場恐續呈高波震盪。
市場劇震後，首爾監管思路從「提示風險」轉向「控增量、消化存量」，暫停新單股槓桿產品上市並禁廣告。自上周五起，散戶新買或加碼境內外單股槓桿產品，帳戶須留至少 3000 萬韓元現金 (原門檻 1000 萬)，股票、債券、一般 ETF 不再計入，個人投資上限、模擬交易、提高過度交易成本等也在研議。
上周五大反彈為市場換來喘息，但從高點跌逾 80% 的槓桿產品需漲逾 400% 才能回本，投資人更在意的是 AI 與半導體敘事是否動搖？
FXTM 富拓特約分析師黃俊指出，本輪是「估值正常回調＋槓桿快進快出」的疊加，若踩踏緩解，韓股仍望平穩，預計 2026 年全球 AI 淨利達 6370 億美元，南韓記憶體類股可沾光。
高盛報告亦提到，南韓今年 6 月工業生產月增 6.4%，優於預期，半導體產量月增率 4.5%，與汽車合貢工業增量四成。
多位機構人士認為：近期下跌以「殺估值」為主，若資金面企穩、未演變成「殺邏輯」「殺盈利」，市場將逐步回歸基本面，野村則把當前去槓桿視為「重置」而非趨勢逆轉，預期韓股從「槓桿牛」切往「企業回購牛」，2026 年韓企回購規模創高、兩大半導體佔九成，KOSPI 萬點目標未廢。
過去 40 天的驚魂揭穿一件事：當一國指數被兩檔半導體與其槓桿衍生品綁架，漲時是流動性奇蹟，跌時是流動性陷阱，接下來的問題不再是「會不會再漲 18%」，而是散戶槓桿出清後，三星與海力士的 HBM 獲利、企業回購、全球 AI 資本開支能否接住這根定價權的棒子。
paras_en: In the past 40 days the Korean market has played out an extreme script: from June 23 to July 30 the KOSPI fell almost 40%, wiping out more than KRW 2,800 trillion of market value – a size that would surpass South Korea’s entire 2025 GDP – and some individual stocks tied to 2× leveraged products retreated more than 80% from their peaks.

A dramatic turn occurred last Friday (July 31) when the KOSPI rebounded nearly 18% in a single day, Samsung Electronics jumped 26.81%, SK Hynix briefly hit the 30% daily limit, and certain 2× long leveraged ETFs surged over 60% – the biggest one‑day gain on record – but the rally also heightened market anxiety: is this a “dead‑cat bounce” at the tail end of de‑leveraging, or a prelude to fundamentals taking over pricing?

The seeds were sown in May when South Korea launched 2× leveraged ETFs that track the daily performance of Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix. When the market rises, the profit‑making effect draws in capital; when it falls, the funds must mechanically unwind positions to maintain the fixed leverage, compounded by margin‑call liquidations, pushing the market into a negative feedback loop.
According to data from the Korea Financial Investment Association, from early May to July 29 brokers forced the sale of about KRW 2.6 trillion of unsettled funds.

Goldman Sachs data released on Saturday (the 1st) shows that as of last Friday the assets of Korean leveraged ETFs fell from a peak of $53 billion to $24 billion, and leveraged holdings as a share of free‑float stocks dropped to 1.9%. After a week or two of outflows, retail investors have started adding back, so daily rebalancing flows, though about half of the peak, “still have a significant impact.”

Huatai Securities says the Korean market’s de‑leveraging is now in its “last mile,” but tail‑end risks remain: first, leveraged‑ETF positions are still relatively high, with U.S. Nvidia and Tesla‑related products accounting for about 0.4% of free‑float market value – a proportion that is clearly excessive for Korea; second, the shrinkage in size has come mainly from price declines of the underlying stocks rather than redemptions, so secondary‑market buying pressure has not cooled; third, the KOSPI‑200 volatility index (VKOSPI) was at the 99.6th percentile of its history since 2005 as of last Thursday.

Huatai estimates that leveraged ETFs still represent 11.4% of the average daily turnover of Samsung and Hynix shares, making them a core source of high volatility. The market is likely to stay volatile until policy measures are implemented in mid‑August.

After the market shock, Seoul regulators have shifted from “risk warnings” to “controlling inflows and digesting existing exposure.” New single‑stock leveraged products are paused from listing and advertising is banned. Starting last Friday, retail investors who buy or add to domestic or overseas single‑stock leveraged products must keep at least KRW 30 million in cash in their accounts (up from the previous KRW 10 million), and holdings of stocks, bonds, or regular ETFs no longer count toward that buffer. Personal investment caps, simulated‑trading limits, and higher transaction costs for excessive trading are also under discussion.

The big rebound on Friday gave the market a brief breather, but leveraged products that have fallen more than 80% from their highs would need to rise over 400% just to break even. Investors are now more concerned about whether the AI and semiconductor narratives can hold up.

FXTM analyst Huang Jun notes that this round is a combination of “normal valuation pull‑back plus rapid in‑and‑out of leverage.” If the panic eases, the Korean market can remain stable. He forecasts global AI net profit to reach $637 billion in 2026, with South Korean memory‑chip stocks benefiting.

Goldman’s report also mentions that South Korea’s industrial production grew 6.4% month‑on‑month in June, beating expectations, with semiconductor output up 4.5% and automotive‑related industries contributing about 40% of the industrial increase.

Several institutional voices say the recent decline has been driven mainly by “valuation killing.” If funding conditions stabilize and the sell‑off does not turn into a “logic kill” or “profit kill,” the market will gradually revert to fundamentals. Nomura views the current de‑leveraging as a “reset” rather than a trend reversal, expecting Korean equities to shift from a “leveraged bull” to an “corporate‑buyback bull,” with 2026 corporate buybacks hitting record levels, two major chipmakers accounting for 90% of the activity, and the KOSPI’s ten‑point target still intact.

The 40‑day nightmare reveals one thing: when a nation’s index is hijacked by two semiconductor stocks and their leveraged derivatives, the rally becomes a liquidity miracle and the crash a liquidity trap. The next question is no longer “Will it rise another 18%?” but whether, after retail leverage is cleared, Samsung’s and Hynix’s HBM profits, corporate buybacks, and global AI cap‑ex can seize the pricing power baton.

items.title: 美股修正「觸底」了嗎？AI股崩跌後迎反彈、晶片股能否迎來新一波行情
items.title_en: Has the US Stock Market Hit Bottom?
paras: 美股上週五（31 日）為過去六週的動盪行情畫下一個戲劇性的句點。近期遭到重創的動能類股連兩個交易日強勁反彈，為這波跌勢暫時止血，也讓市場開始討論，這波修正是否已經探底。
根據《MarketWatch》報導，這波反彈的導火線，是市場傳出一檔操作積極、槓桿程度極高、專注人工智慧（AI）題材的避險基金出清其股票部位。
消息一出，半導體類股應聲大漲，道瓊市場數據顯示，這是晶片股自六月以來最強勁的兩日漲幅。
然而，即便有最後一刻的絕地反攻，晶片股與其他熱門動能標的七月全月來看仍是重挫收場。分析指出，這顯示指數表面的平靜之下，其實暗藏一場規模不小的個股殺盤。
那斯達克綜合指數七月下跌約 3%，創下三月以來最差單月表現，也是連續第二個月下跌；標普 500 指數同樣連兩個月收黑，但跌幅相對輕微，距六月初創下的歷史高點仍不算太遠。
《彭博》資料顯示，追蹤高波動動能股的高盛高貝塔動量籃子，七月創下 2000 年 11 月以來最差單月表現。該籃子中大量原本作多的部位遭到重擊，反而是放空部位，包括多檔受創嚴重的軟體股逆勢走揚。
Horizon Investments 研究主管 Michael Dickson 指出，在由 Leopold Aschenbrenner 操盤的 AI 新創避險基金 Situational Awareness 爆倉之後，被迫平倉賣壓看似已經告一段落，但晶片類股能否就此展開持續性反彈，仍有待觀察。
他說：「真正的問題是，我們是否已經走到這波動能股輪動的谷底?」

基本面靠邊站，資金瘋狂轉向

這波 AI 交易的鬆動，最早可追溯至六月。此前，包括美光科技 (MU-US) 在內的記憶體概念股在四、五月已呈現噴出走勢，漲勢過熱的隱憂逐漸浮現。
原本市場期待第二季財報季能為 AI 題材注入新動能，結果卻大失所望。即便 Google 母公司 Alphabet(GOOGL-US) 等雲端巨頭證實仍將投入數千億美元擴建 AI 基礎設施，但受惠於 AI 建設瓶頸的半導體、電力、工業類股等相關族群，股價依然疲弱不振。
當企業獲利與資本支出計畫等基本面因素逐漸被市場忽視，資金開始大規模轉向，從晶片股撤出，湧入近期較為冷門的軟體、金融、不動產等類股。
同一時間，油價回升也帶動能源類股七月繳出亮眼漲幅。蘋果 (AAPL-US) 則是另一個受到矚目的個股，其股價七月一度大漲，卻在月底最後一個交易日，因財報表現令投資人失望而回吐大半漲幅。
滙豐銀行策略師 Max Kettern 在報告中直言：「過去六週，基本面因素完全被拋諸腦後。」不過他也指出，股市的技術面正在轉好，顯示本週晶片股與整體動能因子的反彈可能會延續下去。
標普 500 指數上週五收盤重新站上 50 日均線，先前該指數曾短暫跌破此一關鍵支撐。
與此同時，市場恐慌指標 VIX 同樣快速降溫，上週稍早一度衝破 20，週五已回落至 15.99。VIX 來到 20 時已高於長期平均值，顯示七月的動能股拋售潮終於開始對整體指數層級的波動性造成實質衝擊。
期間，市場贏家與輸家之間的分歧一度擴大到歷史罕見的程度，標普 500 成分股間的表現離散度創下紀錄新高區間。
然而，下個月市場能否重回普漲格局，目前仍是未知數。

部分策略師看到轉折訊號

Nationwide 首席市場策略師 Mark Hackett 認為，市場已出現觸底轉折的跡象。舉例來說，高盛高貝塔動量籃子的單月平均每日波動幅度，七月飆升至 2020 年以來新高。
Hackett 指出，這項波動指標過去在幾個重要轉折點也曾出現同樣飆升，包括新冠疫情拋售潮、網路泡沫高點，以及 2008 年金融海嘯後市場落底之時。
Shell Capital 投資長 Mike Shell 則表示，根據其往來主要券商提供的數據，這波動能股平倉賣壓可能已接近尾聲，而非才剛開始。
他強調，這不代表股價已經確定觸底，但風險與報酬的天平確實開始轉向較有利的一方。
Shell 表示：「現在真正的問題是，這波去槓桿究竟是暴露了基本面的問題，還是只是在清洗一筆過度擁擠的交易部位。」
他指出：「如果 AI 需求、企業獲利與資本支出依然穩健，我會把這波回檔視為逢低布局最強 AI 公司的機會。」
儘管如此，投資人對未來一、兩個月的股市表現仍不能掉以輕心。Carson Group 首席市場策略師 Ryan Detrick 在社群平台 X 上提醒，八、九月向來是全年表現最弱的兩個月份。
因此，市場接下來要問的問題是，今年往常出現在夏末的波動，是否已經提前在七月上演完畢?
paras_en: The US stock market ended last week with a dramatic flourish, as momentum stocks that had been heavily beaten down rebounded strongly for two consecutive trading days, temporarily halting the decline and sparking discussions about whether the correction has bottomed out.

According to MarketWatch, the catalyst for the rebound was the liquidation of stocks by a hedge fund that focuses on artificial intelligence (AI) and has high leverage. The news triggered a significant surge in semiconductor stocks, with the Dow Jones Market Data showing that this was the strongest two-day gain for chip stocks since June.

Despite the last-minute rebound, chip stocks and other popular momentum stocks still ended July on a dismal note. Analysts point out that this indicates a significant sell-off in individual stocks beneath the surface of the index's calm appearance.

The Nasdaq Composite Index fell about 3% in July, its worst monthly performance since March, and its second consecutive monthly decline. The S&P 500 Index also fell for the second consecutive month, although its decline was relatively mild and not far from its historic high in early June.

Bloomberg data shows that the Goldman Sachs High Beta Momentum Basket, which tracks high-volatility momentum stocks, had its worst monthly performance since November 2000. The basket's long positions were heavily hit, while its short positions, including several software stocks that were severely damaged, bucked the trend and rose.

Michael Dickson, research director at Horizon Investments, noted that after the AI startup hedge fund Situational Awareness, managed by Leopold Aschenbrenner, blew up, the forced selling pressure seems to have subsided, but it remains to be seen whether chip stocks can sustain a rebound.
He said, 'The real question is, have we reached the bottom of this momentum stock rotation?'

The fundamentals have been ignored, and funds have gone crazy shifting towards other sectors. This wave of AI trading began to loosen up in June, when memory concept stocks, including Micron Technology (MU-US), showed a surge in April and May, raising concerns about overheating.

Initially, the market expected the second-quarter earnings season to inject new momentum into AI-themed stocks, but the results were disappointing. Even though Google's parent company Alphabet (GOOGL-US) and other cloud giants confirmed that they would invest tens of billions of dollars in expanding AI infrastructure, the related stocks, including semiconductors, power, and industrial stocks, remained weak.

As corporate earnings and capital expenditure plans were gradually ignored by the market, funds began to shift significantly, withdrawing from chip stocks and pouring into software, finance, and real estate stocks, which had been relatively cold until recently.

At the same time, the rebound in oil prices also drove energy stocks to post impressive gains in July. Apple (AAPL-US) was another stock that received attention, with its stock price surging in July before retreating significantly on the last trading day of the month due to disappointing earnings.

HSBC strategist Max Kettern said in a report, 'Over the past six weeks, fundamental factors have been completely ignored.' However, he also pointed out that the technical aspect of the stock market is improving, indicating that the rebound in chip stocks and overall momentum factors may continue this week.
The S&P 500 Index closed above its 50-day moving average on Friday, after briefly falling below this key support level earlier.

Meanwhile, the market fear index VIX also cooled down quickly, falling to 15.99 on Friday after briefly surpassing 20 earlier in the week. When the VIX reaches 20, it is higher than its long-term average, indicating that the momentum stock sell-off in July finally began to have a significant impact on the overall index's volatility.

During this period, the disparity between the winners and losers in the market expanded to a historically rare degree, with the performance gap between S&P 500 constituent stocks reaching a record high.
However, it remains to be seen whether the market can return to a broad uptrend next month.

Some strategists see a turning point. Nationwide's chief market strategist Mark Hackett believes that the market has shown signs of a bottom. For example, the average daily volatility of the Goldman Sachs High Beta Momentum Basket surged to a new high since 2020 in July.

Hackett pointed out that this volatility indicator has also surged at several important turning points in the past, including the coronavirus sell-off, the peak of the internet bubble, and the bottom of the market after the 2008 financial crisis.
Mike Shell, investment manager at Shell Capital, said that according to data from major brokers, the forced selling pressure on momentum stocks may be nearing its end, rather than just beginning.
He emphasized that this does not mean that stock prices have definitely bottomed, but the risk-reward balance has begun to shift in a more favorable direction.
Shell said, 'Now the real question is, did this deleveraging expose fundamental problems or just wash out an overcrowded trade?'
He pointed out, 'If AI demand, corporate earnings, and capital expenditure plans remain robust, I would view this pullback as an opportunity to buy into the strongest AI companies at a low price.'

However, investors should still be cautious about the market's performance in the next one or two months. Carson Group's chief market strategist Ryan Detrick warned on social media platform X that August and September are usually the weakest months of the year.
Therefore, the market is wondering whether the usual summer volatility has already been played out in July.

items.title: 晨星看好輝達仍被低估！目標價280美元、潛在漲幅40%
items.title_en: Morningstar Sees Nvidia Still Undervalued! Target Price $280, Potential Upside 40%
paras: 過去幾年，輝達 (NVDA-US) 幾乎是市場上最不吝於給出高溢價的一檔股票。不過自 5 月中旬以來，受到超大規模雲端業者資本支出可能放緩的疑慮影響，輝達股價已下滑約 17%，讓晨星罕見地將其歸類為「被低估」的標的。
根據《Business Insider》報導，晨星在近日發布的報告中指出，輝達的合理價值評估為每股 280 美元，相較上週五（31 日）200.75 美元的收盤價，仍有約 40% 的上漲空間。
晨星認為，支撐這項評價的核心因素有二。首先是輝達擁有寬廣的「經濟護城河」，其 GPU 晶片、CUDA 軟體生態系及相關產品，在市場上仍具有難以取代的技術優勢。
其次，隨著各大雲端服務業者持續加碼投資 AI 基礎建設，晨星預期輝達營收將維持強勁成長動能，甚至看好其 2027 年營收成長率可達 80%。
值得注意的是，自 2023 年初以來，晨星對輝達的合理價值估算大致與其實際股價同步變動，但自去年 10 月起，兩者出現明顯分歧。
儘管晨星認為輝達目前股價仍遭低估，但同時也給予該股「非常高」的不確定性評級。
晨星指出，其中一項風險在於，作為輝達最大客戶的超大規模雲端服務供應商，未來可能逐步自行開發 AI 硬體。不過，晨星認為，這些自研產品短期內不太可能與輝達形成直接競爭，更難以完全取代其產品。
另一項主要風險則是，超大規模雲端業者可能因應投資人壓力，而縮減 AI 資本支出。
上週， Meta(META-US) 就因上調資本支出預測而遭到市場拋售，微軟 (MSFT-US) 則因維持原有支出計畫而獲得投資人青睞。不過，Meta 財報表現未達市場預期，而微軟則交出優於預期的財報，這也是兩家公司股價走勢分化的重要因素。
儘管如此，晨星仍不認為 AI 基礎建設投資將在短期內降溫。
晨星資深股票分析師 Brian Colello 在報告中表示：「鑑於 AI 資本支出短期與中期極有可能維持強勁，甚至長期也有望持續成長，我們認為市場低估了輝達的成長前景。」
他並補充表示：「目前這檔股票看起來很划算。」
paras_en: In recent years, Nvidia (NVDA-US) has been one of the market’s most generous stocks in terms of premium. However, since mid‑May, concerns that massive cloud providers may slow their capital spending have knocked the share price down about 17%, prompting Morningstar to unusually label it as an "undervalued" stock.
According to Business Insider, Morningstar’s latest report values Nvidia at a fair price of $280 per share, which implies roughly a 40% upside from last Friday’s (the 31st) closing price of $200.75.

Morningstar says two core factors support this valuation. First, Nvidia enjoys a broad economic moat: its GPU chips, CUDA software ecosystem and related products retain a technically superior position that is hard to replace in the market.

Second, as major cloud service providers continue to pour money into AI infrastructure, Morningstar expects Nvidia’s revenue to keep strong growth momentum and even forecasts an 80% revenue growth rate by 2027.

It is worth noting that since early 2023 Morningstar’s fair‑value estimates for Nvidia have generally moved in line with the actual stock price, but a clear divergence has emerged since October last year.
Although Morningstar believes Nvidia’s current price is still undervalued, it also assigns the stock a "very high" uncertainty rating.

One risk highlighted is that the largest customers—massive cloud service providers—might gradually develop their own AI hardware. Morningstar, however, thinks these in‑house products are unlikely to directly compete with Nvidia in the short term and are far from fully replacing its offerings.
Another major risk is that huge cloud operators could cut AI capital spending in response to investor pressure.

Last week, Meta (META-US) was sold off after raising its capital‑spending outlook, while Microsoft (MSFT-US) won investor favor by sticking to its existing spending plan. Meta’s earnings missed market expectations, whereas Microsoft delivered better‑than‑expected results, which helped explain the divergent stock moves.
Nevertheless, Morningstar does not think AI infrastructure investment will cool off in the short term.

Senior equity analyst Brian Colello said in the report: "Given that AI capital spending is very likely to remain strong in the short and medium term, and may even continue to grow in the long term, we believe the market is underestimating Nvidia’s growth prospects."
He added: "At the moment this stock looks like a very good deal."

items.title: 投資人的通膨時代投資指南！法興銀行列「7大」抗通膨資產
items.title_en: Investor's Inflation‑Era Investment Guide! Societe Generale Lists Seven Anti‑Inflation Assets
paras: 美國通膨數據可能再度升溫，讓市場神經緊繃。不過法國興業銀行分析師認為，投資人仍有幾處可以躲避風暴的角落，並據此開出一套七項資產組成的避險策略。
根據《Business Insider》報導，過去幾年通膨降溫趨勢原本相對明朗，但邁入 2026 年後，情勢似乎出現逆轉。伊朗戰事的外溢效應，加上美國總統川普祭出的關稅措施，都讓市場重新評估物價上漲的風險。
更令投資人不安的，是聯準會（Fed）領導層更替所帶來的政策不確定性。市場對聯準會能否將通膨壓回 2% 目標的信心正在流失。
聯準會主席華許（Kevin Warsh）上週宣布維持利率不變。然而，即便油價近期明顯反彈，他仍堅持央行不應對未來利率路徑提供明確指引，進一步加劇了市場的焦慮情緒。
法興銀行在近日發布的客戶報告中指出，聯準會偏好的通膨指標核心個人消費支出（PCE）物價指數，目前的預期水準「仍高於平順回歸目標所應對應的路徑」，且該指標已連續超過五年高於 2% 的官方目標。
報告寫道：「總體經濟基本面持續支撐通膨的頑固性，第二波美國關稅、加速擴張的 AI 與基礎建設資本支出循環、油價波動再起，加上已開發經濟體普遍居高不下的財政赤字都顯示，通膨環境恐比市場目前定價的還要嚴峻。」
基於此，法興銀行列出七項可望在通膨環境下表現不俗的資產類別，作為投資人的避險參考。

一、抗通膨美國公債

抗通膨美國公債（TIPS）是一種會依據通膨變化調整本金的美國政府公債，其本金每半年依據最新通膨數據進行調整。
在通膨環境下，TIPS 通常被視為避險資產之一，能為投資人提供相對穩定的報酬，且隨著通膨升溫，其本金與利息給付也會同步增加。
法興銀行策略師在報告中表示：「TIPS 仍是我們最偏好的直接抗通膨工具。」
策略師指出：「目前實際通膨率仍高於市場定價，而法興銀行經濟學家預估，2026 年核心個人消費支出年增率仍將維持在 3% 以上，因此重新布局抗通膨資產的理由依然相當充分。」
提供 TIPS 投資部位的安碩抗通膨債券 ETF(TIP-US) 今年以來已下跌約 2%。
值得注意的是，債券價格與殖利率呈反向變動，因此該 ETF 價格下跌，代表實質殖利率正在上升。

二、歐洲抗通膨公債

歐洲抗通膨公債，是歐洲市場對抗通膨政府公債的通稱，可視為美國抗通膨公債的對應產品。
法興銀行表示，歐洲抗通膨公債為投資人提供了具吸引力的抗通膨配置機會，有助於提升投資組合的抗通膨能力。
報告指出：「法國與西班牙的抗通膨公債估值仍具吸引力，而義大利長天期抗通膨公債同樣具有投資價值。此外，投資人需求強勁，也為這類資產帶來進一步支撐。」

三、銅

法興銀行將銅稱為「實體經濟中的抗通膨避險資產」。
該行策略師在報告中指出：「電氣化、AI 基礎建設以及電力網路擴張持續推升銅需求，但礦業投資仍相對低迷。在結構性需求強勁與供給受限的雙重支撐下，銅價長期展望仍然樂觀。」
近期，隨著投資人開始關注 AI 熱潮背後的實體供應限制，銅再度成為市場焦點。
今年以來，銅價已較年初水準上漲約 14%，並延續 2025 年以來的強勁漲勢。

四、黃金

黃金作為傳統避險資產，長期以來也被市場視為對抗通膨的重要工具，因此同樣被法興銀行列入推薦名單。
該行將黃金稱為「對抗政策不確定性的戰略性避險工具」，意指地緣政治風險以及利率走勢的不確定性，也可能推升金價。
法興銀行表示：「市場對聯準會維持高利率更長時間的預期，已有很大部分反映在價格之中。ETF 需求仍保持正向，金價波動率已下降，而各國央行持續推動外匯儲備多元化，將為金價提供長期且穩定的支撐。」
今年以來，黃金價格下跌約 5%，主要是在 2025 年底出現一波狂熱上漲後，市場情緒逐漸降溫。

五、大宗商品與實體經濟類股

法興銀行也看好與實體經濟相關的股票機會，例如大宗商品、工業股與原材料類股。
該行指出，作為其偏好的「分散化商品曝險工具」之一，彭博商品總報酬指數（Bloomberg Commodity Total Return Index）今年以來已上漲 18%，表現優於標普 500 指數。
策略師進一步表示，該行也偏好標普 500 等權重指數，因為其「更清晰地表達了我們對實體經濟的正面看法」。
原因在於，等權重指數中配置較高比例的實體經濟類股；相較之下，以市值加權計算的標普 500 指數，目前高度集中於科技股。

六、歐洲公債與銀行、公共事業股

法興銀行也看好歐洲主權公債，以及銀行股與公用事業股的投資機會，尤其是在歐盟整體財政狀況逐步改善的背景下，這些資產有望受惠。
該行策略師指出：「邊陲國家目前已開始實現基本財政盈餘，而多數核心國家仍處於財政赤字狀態，這推動市場持續上調對邊陲國家的信用評級。」
策略師進一步表示，歐洲地區「財政基本面正在改善」，且預期經濟增長將更加強勁。

七、私募信貸

法興銀行表示，儘管近期市場對私募信貸的疑慮升溫，但此類資產仍可透過其浮動利率結構，發揮「天然抗通膨避險工具」的作用。
策略師指出，由於私募信貸投資收益率通常會隨著市場利率變動，因此當金融市場利率維持高檔時，相關投資的收益率也有機會同步上升。
法興銀行表示：「由於直接放貸約占私募信貸市場 70%，在利率維持高檔更長時間的環境下，將直接轉化為更高的票息收入，使私募信貸成為抗通膨投資策略中的自然補充配置。」
不過，近期私募信貸基金也面臨壓力。市場擔憂軟體產業與 AI 領域可能出現風險擴散效應，導致投資人掀起一波贖回申請潮。
包括黑石 (BX-US) 、貝萊德 (BLK-US) 、Apollo Global Management (APO-US) 以及 KKR (KKR-US) 等大型業者，都受到這波市場動盪影響。
paras_en: U.S. inflation data may heat up again, keeping markets on edge. However, analysts at Societe Generale say investors still have a few safe‑havens to dodge the storm, and they have drafted a seven‑asset hedging strategy.

According to Business Insider, the recent years’ cooling‑inflation trend had been fairly clear, but after entering 2026 the situation appears to be reversing. Spill‑over effects from the Iran war and tariff measures introduced by U.S. President Trump have prompted the market to reassess price‑rise risks.
What worries investors even more is the policy uncertainty caused by changes in the Federal Reserve leadership. Confidence that the Fed can push inflation back to its 2% target is eroding.

Fed Chair Kevin Warsh announced last week that rates would stay unchanged. Yet even as oil prices have rebounded sharply, he insisted the central bank should not give a clear forward‑guidance on the rate path, further stoking market anxiety.

Societe Generale’s recent client report notes that the Fed‑preferred inflation gauge – core personal consumption expenditures (PCE) – is still expected to be “above the smooth‑return‑to‑target path,” and the metric has stayed above the 2% official goal for more than five consecutive years.

The report states: “The overall economic fundamentals continue to underpin stubborn inflation. The second wave of U.S. tariffs, the accelerating AI and infrastructure‑capex cycle, renewed oil‑price volatility, and persistently high fiscal deficits in developed economies all suggest that the inflation environment may be harsher than the market currently prices in.”
Based on this, Societe Generale lists seven asset classes that could perform well in an inflationary setting as hedging references for investors.
1. Inflation‑Protected U.S. Treasury Bonds
U.S. Treasury Inflation‑Protected Securities (TIPS) are government bonds that adjust their principal according to inflation, with the principal re‑indexed every six months based on the latest data.
In an inflationary environment, TIPS are generally viewed as a hedge, offering investors relatively stable returns, and both principal and interest payments rise as inflation climbs.
Societe Generale strategists wrote in the report: “TIPS remain our top‑preferred direct anti‑inflation tool.”

The strategists added: “Real inflation is still above market pricing, and our economists project that core PCE growth will stay above 3% in 2026, so there is ample reason to re‑allocate toward inflation‑protected assets.”
The anti‑inflation bond ETF TIP‑US, which provides exposure to TIPS, has fallen about 2% year‑to‑date.
Note that bond prices move inversely to yields, so the ETF’s price decline indicates that real yields are rising.
2. European Inflation‑Linked Sovereign Bonds
European inflation‑linked sovereign bonds are the continent’s counterpart to U.S. TIPS, representing government debt that adjusts for inflation.
Societe Generale says these bonds offer attractive inflation‑hedging opportunities and can boost a portfolio’s resilience to price pressures.

The report notes: “French and Spanish inflation‑linked bonds remain attractively valued, and long‑dated Italian inflation‑linked securities also have investment merit. Strong investor demand further supports these assets.”
3. Copper
Societe Generale calls copper a “real‑economy anti‑inflation hedge.”

The bank’s strategists write: “Electrification, AI infrastructure and power‑grid expansion are continuously lifting copper demand, while mining investment remains relatively weak. With strong structural demand and constrained supply, the long‑term outlook for copper prices stays upbeat.”
Recently, as investors focus on the physical supply constraints behind the AI boom, copper has re‑emerged as a market focus.
Copper prices are up roughly 14% since the start of the year, continuing the strong rally that began in 2025.
4. Gold
Gold, a traditional safe‑haven, has long been viewed as a key tool against inflation and is also on Societe Generale’s recommendation list.
The bank describes gold as a “strategic hedge against policy uncertainty,” meaning that geopolitical risks and unclear rate trajectories can also lift gold prices.

Societe Generale states: “Market expectations that the Fed will keep rates high for longer are already reflected in prices. ETF demand remains positive, gold volatility has fallen, and central banks’ ongoing diversification of foreign‑exchange reserves will provide long‑term, stable support for gold.”
Gold prices have fallen about 5% year‑to‑date, after a frenzy of buying at the end of 2025 cooled market sentiment.
5. Commodities and Real‑Economy Stocks
Societe Generale is also bullish on stocks tied to the real economy, such as commodity, industrial and raw‑material equities.
The bank notes that its preferred “diversified commodity‑exposure tool,” the Bloomberg Commodity Total Return Index, is up 18% year‑to‑date, outperforming the S&P 500.
Strategists further say they favor an equal‑weight S&P 500 index because it “more clearly reflects our positive view on the real economy.”
The reasoning is that an equal‑weight index gives a higher weighting to real‑economy stocks, whereas the market‑cap‑weighted S&P 500 is currently heavily concentrated in technology firms.
6. European Sovereign Bonds, Bank and Utility Stocks
Societe Generale also sees opportunities in European sovereign bonds as well as bank and utility equities, especially as the overall fiscal situation in the EU gradually improves.
Strategists comment: “Peripheral countries have begun to post basic fiscal surpluses, while many core nations remain in deficit, prompting markets to upgrade credit ratings for the periphery.”
They add that Europe’s “fiscal fundamentals are improving” and that economic growth is expected to pick up.
7. Private‑Credit
Although recent market concerns about private credit have risen, Societe Generale says the asset class can act as a “natural inflation‑hedge” thanks to its floating‑rate structure.
Strategists note that private‑credit returns typically move with market rates, so when rates stay elevated, yields on these investments can rise in tandem.

The bank states: “Since direct lending accounts for roughly 70% of the private‑credit market, a prolonged high‑rate environment translates directly into higher coupon income, making private credit a natural complement to an inflation‑focused strategy.”
However, private‑credit funds are under pressure lately. Markets fear that risk could spill from the software and AI sectors, prompting a wave of redemption requests.
Large players such as Blackstone (BX‑US), BlackRock (BLK‑US), Apollo Global Management (APO‑US) and KKR (KKR‑US) have all been affected by this market turbulence.

items.title: 貝森特本周還「救市」？美日韓近30年最大規模聯手干預匯市 穩AI盟友資產防風險外溢
items.title_en: Did Bessemer Rescue the Market This Week? US, Japan, and South Korea Launch Largest Coordinated FX Intervention in 30 Years to Shield AI Allies' Assets from Risk Spillover
paras: 上週，美國、日本、韓國三方罕見聯手，實施近 30 年來最大規模的協調外匯干預行動，不只壓制日元、韓元貶值，更被市場解讀為美國穩住盟友金融市場、防止亞洲資產波動倒灌華爾街的「聯合救市」。
東京當局上周四 (7 月 30 日) 單日動用約 8.45 兆日元 (約 528 億美元) 拋售美元、買入日元，規模居史上前列，同日南韓外匯當局也罕見入市拋美元，韓元單日升值 2% 至 9 個月高點。
隔天，美國財政部透過紐約聯準銀行委託高盛、摩根士丹利「賣歐元、買日元」，為 1998 年來美國首次直接參與日元干預。三方出手後，美元兌日元自 162 上方摔落至 157—159 區間，日元脫離 40 年低點。
美國下場方式極具技術性。正式交易前，紐約聯準銀行連兩日先做「匯率檢查」，上周四查美元兌日元、上周五查歐元兌日元，只問價不成交，釋放信號。
美銀外匯策略師 Alex Cohen 指出，「匯率檢查」介於口頭喊話與真金白銀之間，是美國財政部今年新用的壓力工具，選歐元通道而非美元通道，意在挺日元同時不增美元供給、護住美元指數。
南韓副財長 Moon Ji-sung 證實與美日密切協調，日本財務省副大臣三村淳直言，美方支持「已超越單純道義聲援」。背景是日韓市場同步承壓，KOSDAQ 摔到 2022 年 10 月以來低點，科技股去槓桿未完，日元韓元續弱恐引發亞洲資產連鎖重估。
華爾街更關注「為什麼是現在」。美銀策略師 Hartnett 將此次行動稱為 AI 時代「價格維持操作」(PKO)，因日韓皆為美國半導體與 AI 供應鏈核心，三星、SK 海力士、東京電子牽動全球算力擴張，若本幣崩貶推高日債收益率、逼出套利交易平倉，火會燒到美債與美股。美
因此，美國要降三大類風險：防日元急貶炸日債利率、防金融壓力擴散亞洲、防無序資本流衝擊美債。今年以來，半導體 ETF 吸金約 530 億美元，費半指數短線回檔，但 AI 資本開支邏輯未破，華府不願盟友資產在槓桿尾聲被空頭收割。
不過干預≠趨勢反轉。匯率檢查能嚇退投機，但若日美利差未收、韓股去槓桿未淨，日元韓元仍可能被重新測試。
市場共識是：這輪協調先把「無序貶值」按住，替 8 月南韓監管落地、日本央行 (BOJ) 下月利率評估買時間，真正定價權回歸，仍看半導體獲利、企業回購與全球 AI 開支。
近 30 年首見的美方直接下場，訊號意義已大過金額本身，華府把日韓匯率與資產穩定，正式列為本土金融防線的一環。
paras_en: Last week, the United States, Japan and South Korea unusually joined forces to carry out the largest coordinated foreign‑exchange intervention in nearly three decades. The operation not only curbed the yen and won’s depreciation but was also read by the market as a joint "rescue" aimed at stabilising allied financial markets and preventing Asian asset volatility from spilling over onto Wall Street.

On Thursday, July 30, Tokyo authorities sold roughly ¥8.45 trillion (about $52.8 billion) of dollars and bought yen in a single‑day operation, a scale that ranks among the biggest in history. On the same day, South Korean foreign‑exchange officials also entered the market to sell dollars, pushing the won up 2% to a nine‑month high.

The next day, the US Treasury, via the New York Federal Reserve Bank and through Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley, sold euros and bought yen – marking the first time since 1998 that the United States directly participated in yen intervention. After the three‑way action, the dollar‑yen rate fell from above 162 to the 157‑159 band, pulling the yen out of a 40‑year low.

The US’s exit strategy was highly technical. Before any trades were executed, the New York Fed conducted two days of “rate checks”: on Thursday it probed the dollar‑yen pair, and on Friday the euro‑yen pair, asking for quotes without actually transacting, thereby sending a signal to the market.

Bank of America foreign‑exchange strategist Alex Cohen explained that a “rate check” sits between a verbal warning and a real trade, and is a new pressure tool the Treasury has adopted this year. By targeting the euro‑yen channel rather than the dollar‑yen channel, the US aimed to support the yen without increasing dollar supply and to protect the dollar index.

South Korean Deputy Finance Minister Moon Ji‑sung confirmed close coordination with the US and Japan, while Japanese Ministry of Finance Vice‑Minister Mitsumura Jun‑nao said US support had "gone beyond a purely moral endorsement." The backdrop was simultaneous pressure on both markets: the KOSDAQ had fallen to its lowest level since October 2022, tech‑stock deleveraging was still underway, and continued weakness in the yen and won risked triggering a chain‑reaction revaluation of Asian assets.

Wall Street was more focused on "why now." Bank of America strategist Hartnett labelled the move a price‑maintenance operation (PKO) for the AI era, noting that both Japan and South Korea are core to the US semiconductor and AI supply chain – companies like Samsung, SK Hynix and Tokyo Electron drive global compute expansion. A collapse of their currencies could push Japanese bond yields higher and force arbitrage unwindings, which would then spread to US Treasuries and equities.

Thus, the US aims to reduce three major risks: preventing a sharp yen drop that would spike Japanese bond yields, containing financial stress from spilling across Asia, and averting disorderly capital flows that could hit US bonds. Since the start of the year, semiconductor ETFs have attracted about $53 billion, the semiconductor index has pulled back in the short term, but the logic of AI‑driven capital spending remains intact, and Washington does not want its allies’ assets to be harvested by short‑sellers at the end of the leverage cycle.

However, intervention does not equal a trend reversal. Rate checks can scare off speculators, but if the US‑Japan interest‑rate differential remains unaddressed and Korean equity deleveraging is not resolved, the yen and won could still be tested again.

The market consensus is that this round of coordination first contains "disorderly depreciation," buying time for South Korean regulators to implement August measures and for the Bank of Japan to assess rates next month. True pricing power will return based on semiconductor earnings, corporate buybacks and global AI spending.

The US’s direct involvement – a first in 30 years – carries a signal that outweighs the monetary amount itself. Washington is now treating the stability of Japanese and Korean exchange rates and assets as an integral part of its domestic financial defence line.

items.title: 搶救日元大作戰！日本疑連兩天干預匯市 美財政部、Fed也有動作
items.title_en: Japan's Large-Scale Intervention in the Foreign Exchange Market
paras: 日本政府可能再度大規模進場支撐日元，根據日本央行帳戶數據與市場機構估算，日本當局週四 (30 日) 疑似買進日元、拋售美元，規模約達 8.45 兆日元 (約 528 億美元)。日媒隨後報導，日本週五可能連續第二天干預匯市；同一時間，美國財政部與紐約聯準銀行也傳出採取準備行動，使市場更加相信美日正在協調遏止日元貶勢。
不過，日本與美國政府目前均未正式證實已實際進場，因此現階段仍應表述為「疑似干預」或「市場推測」，不能直接認定美日已聯手買進日元。
週四紐約交易時段，美元兌日元在不到一小時內由 162.5 附近急跌至 158 以下，跌幅一度達 3.3%，創 2023 年 12 月以來最大單日跌幅。這種短時間內集中出現的大幅波動，與日本過去進場干預時的走勢相似，促使交易員迅速鎖定官方可能已經出手。
Totan Research 研究員 Yuichiro Takai 根據日本央行公布的帳戶數據及貨幣經紀商預測，估計日本政府週四可能動用約 8.45 兆日元支撐匯率。他最初估算規模約 9.6 兆日元，納入其他流動性因素後才下修數字，並認為相關數據幾乎可以確定存在干預操作。
如果最終獲得官方證實，這將是日本自 4 月底至 5 月間一輪干預行動後，再度進場捍衛日元，單日規模也可能接近歷史最高水準。
市場對日本連續出手的猜測週五進一步升溫。
《日經新聞》盤後報導，日本央行及相關政府機構已連續第二天買進日元。美元兌日元隨即跌破 157.60，日元升至兩個半月高點，單日升幅約 1.4%。
日本官員並未確認相關消息。財務大臣片山皋月對是否干預表示不予置評。
負責外匯事務的副財務大臣三村淳同樣拒絕說明，但透露日本獲得美國「不僅止於精神層面」的支持。
這番說法被市場解讀為，美方可能已透過實際措施協助日本穩定匯率。
《路透》引述知情人士報導，美國財政部已通知多家銀行，可能於週五進入日元市場，並要求銀行為後續行動做好準備。《彭博》也引述消息人士指出，紐約聯準銀行曾要求至少兩家美國大型銀行提供日元兌歐元報價。
這類「匯率詢價」並不等同實際買賣，但通常被市場視為干預前的準備步驟，可用來掌握流動性、評估交易成本，也能向交易員發出官方密切關注匯率的警告。
紐約聯準銀行拒絕評論，美國財政部也未確認是否準備實際進場。
美國財長貝森特週五 (31 日) 表示，美國財政部與日本政府維持牢固關係及密切協調，並肯定日本首相高市早苗、日本央行行長植田和男及央行理事會維護貨幣與金融穩定的決心。
貝森特先前還表示，日元看起來被「嚴重低估」，過度波動不利於市場正常運作。
前日本央行官員 Nobuyasu Atago 認為，貝森特的表態影響力不可小覷，顯示美國對日本干預匯市的配合意願有所提高。
不過，匯率詢價、口頭支持與實際干預仍屬不同層次。
即使美國財政部真的參與，也尚不清楚會採取直接買進日元、委託紐約聯準銀行執行交易，或僅以詢價及政策訊號配合日本。
從政策背景來看，日本政府先前已投入龐大資金穩定匯率。
財務省數據顯示，4 月 28 日至 5 月 27 日期間，日本累計動用約 11.73 兆日元干預匯市，創下歷史最高紀錄。市場認為，相關資金主要來自出售美元資產及部分美國公債。
然而，上一輪干預並未徹底扭轉日元弱勢。受到美日利差維持高檔及套息交易活躍影響，美元兌日元 7 月 23 日一度升至 163.99，寫下近 40 年新高。
這也顯示，官方買進日元雖能在短期內打亂市場部位，卻未必足以改變由利率差距主導的長期趨勢。
日本央行週五維持政策利率在 1% 不變，符合市場預期。植田和男在記者會上釋出偏鷹訊號，強調通膨上行風險，並表示日本潛在通膨已接近 2% 目標；如果金融環境過度寬鬆，央行不排除加快升息。
植田也指出，匯率變動對通膨的影響正在增強，日本央行必須更加留意日元貶值帶來的價格壓力。然而，由於央行未明確暗示將提前升息，相關談話未能大幅改變市場的政策預期。目前交易員普遍認為，日本央行最快可能在 10 月再次升息，但仍須視通膨、薪資及匯率表現而定。
三菱日聯金融集團外匯策略師 Lee Hardman 表示，美國進行匯率詢價的消息，加劇市場對官方可能再度干預的戒心。高盛則認為，匯市干預雖非可持續的根本解方，卻能在一段時間內降低匯率對經濟週期及利差變化的敏感度；日本也擁有足夠的外匯存底，短期內仍有能力持續進場。
野村國際指出，如果經濟與利率基本面沒有改變，干預對日元的提振作用可能只是暫時的。只要美日利差保持高位，投資人借入低利率日元、買進高收益美元資產的套息交易仍可能延續，限制日元後續升值空間。
因此，這波行情的關鍵已不只是日本是否連續兩天進場，而是美國會否由言語支持進一步轉向實際配合，以及日本央行能否透過升息縮小美日利差。在官方公布完整交易數據以前，8.45 兆日元的規模及美國可能參與干預等說法，仍屬媒體報導與市場推算，尚非官方確認事實。
paras_en: The Japanese government may have intervened in the foreign exchange market for the second consecutive day, according to data from the Bank of Japan and market estimates. On Thursday, Japanese authorities are believed to have bought yen and sold dollars, with a total amount of approximately 8.45 trillion yen (around $528 billion).

The US Department of the Treasury and the Federal Reserve are also reported to have taken preparatory actions, making the market believe that the US and Japan are coordinating to curb the yen's depreciation. However, neither the Japanese nor the US government has officially confirmed the intervention, so it is still described as 'suspected intervention' or 'market speculation'.

On Thursday, during the New York trading session, the dollar-yen exchange rate plummeted from around 162.5 to below 158 within less than an hour, with a drop of 3.3% at one point, the largest single-day decline since December 2023. This sharp fluctuation is similar to the pattern seen when Japan intervened in the foreign exchange market in the past, prompting traders to quickly focus on possible official action.

Yuichiro Takai, a researcher at Totan Research, estimated that the Japanese government may have used around 8.45 trillion yen to support the exchange rate on Thursday, based on the Bank of Japan's account data and forecasts from currency brokers. If officially confirmed, this would be Japan's second intervention in the foreign exchange market since the last round of action in late April to early May, with the single-day scale possibly approaching a historical high.

The market's speculation about Japan's consecutive intervention intensified on Friday. The Nikkei reported that the Bank of Japan and related government agencies had bought yen for the second consecutive day, causing the dollar-yen exchange rate to fall below 157.60, with the yen rising to a two-and-a-half-month high, up about 1.4% on the day.

Japanese officials have not confirmed the reports. Finance Minister Shunichi Suzuki declined to comment on whether there was an intervention. Vice Finance Minister for International Affairs Masayuki Takahashi also refused to explain but revealed that Japan had received support from the US that was 'not just verbal'.

This statement was interpreted by the market as a sign that the US may have taken actual measures to help Japan stabilize the exchange rate. Reuters cited informed sources as saying that the US Department of the Treasury had notified several banks that it may enter the yen market on Friday and asked them to prepare for subsequent actions.

Bloomberg also quoted sources as saying that the New York Federal Reserve had asked at least two major US banks to provide yen-euro quotes. This type of 'exchange rate inquiry' is not equivalent to actual buying and selling but is usually seen as a preparatory step for intervention, which can be used to grasp liquidity, assess transaction costs, and warn traders that officials are closely watching the exchange rate.

The New York Federal Reserve declined to comment, and the US Department of the Treasury did not confirm whether it was preparing to actually intervene. US Treasury Secretary Janet Yellen stated on Friday that the US Department of the Treasury maintained a strong relationship with the Japanese government and was in close coordination, and praised the determination of Japanese Prime Minister Fumio Kishida, Bank of Japan Governor Kazuo Ueda, and the bank's policy board to maintain monetary and financial stability.

Yellen previously stated that the yen appeared to be 'undervalued', and excessive fluctuations were detrimental to the normal functioning of the market. Former Bank of Japan official Nobuyasu Atago believed that Yellen's statement had a significant impact, showing that the US was more willing to cooperate with Japan's intervention in the foreign exchange market.

However, exchange rate inquiries, verbal support, and actual intervention are still different levels. Even if the US Department of the Treasury participates, it is unclear whether it will directly buy yen, commission the New York Federal Reserve to execute transactions, or only cooperate with Japan through inquiries and policy signals.

From a policy perspective, the Japanese government had previously invested a large amount of funds to stabilize the exchange rate. According to data from the Ministry of Finance, between April 28 and May 27, Japan used a total of approximately 11.73 trillion yen to intervene in the foreign exchange market, setting a historical record. The market believes that the funds mainly came from the sale of dollar assets and some US Treasury bonds.

However, the previous round of intervention did not completely reverse the yen's weakness. Due to the high interest rate differential between the US and Japan and active carry trades, the dollar-yen exchange rate rose to 163.99 on July 23, a new high in nearly 40 years.

This also shows that official purchases of yen can disrupt market positions in the short term but may not be enough to change the long-term trend dominated by interest rate differentials. The Bank of Japan maintained its policy rate at 1% on Friday, in line with market expectations.

Bank of Japan Governor Kazuo Ueda sent a hawkish signal at a press conference, emphasizing the risk of rising inflation and stating that Japan's underlying inflation had approached the 2% target. If the financial environment becomes too loose, the bank does not rule out accelerating rate hikes. Ueda also pointed out that the impact of exchange rate fluctuations on inflation was increasing, and the Bank of Japan must pay closer attention to the price pressure brought about by the yen's depreciation.

However, since the bank did not clearly imply that it would raise interest rates ahead of schedule, the remarks did not significantly change the market's policy expectations. Currently, traders generally believe that the Bank of Japan may raise interest rates again in October at the earliest, depending on inflation, wages, and exchange rate performance.

Lee Hardman, a foreign exchange strategist at Mitsubishi UFJ Financial Group, said that the news of the US conducting exchange rate inquiries had intensified the market's concern about possible official intervention. Goldman Sachs believes that foreign exchange market intervention is not a sustainable fundamental solution but can reduce the sensitivity of exchange rates to economic cycles and changes in interest rate differentials for a period. Japan also has sufficient foreign exchange reserves and can continue to intervene in the short term.

Nomura International pointed out that if the economic and interest rate fundamentals do not change, the boosting effect of intervention on the yen may only be temporary. As long as the US-Japan interest rate differential remains high, investors' carry trades of borrowing low-interest yen to buy high-yielding dollar assets may continue, limiting the yen's potential for further appreciation.

Therefore, the key to this trend is no longer just whether Japan intervenes for two consecutive days but whether the US will move from verbal support to actual cooperation and whether the Bank of Japan can narrow the US-Japan interest rate differential through rate hikes. Before the official transaction data is released, the scale of 8.45 trillion yen and the possibility of US participation in the intervention are still media reports and market estimates, not officially confirmed facts.

items.title: 日本保衛日元恐賣美債？干預規模估530億美元 30年期殖利率衝2007年高點
items.title_en: Japan Defends Yen, Risks Selling U.S. Treasuries? Intervention Estimated at $53 B, 30‑Year Yield Hits 2007 High
paras: 日本最新一輪穩定日元匯率的行動，正對美國公債市場帶來重大且可能令人擔憂的影響。
日元兌美元周四 (30 日) 勁升 3.3%，外媒揣測可能是日本政府為了支撐日元而進場干預。依據帳戶資料以及貨幣市場經紀商的預測分析，日本此次干預規模可能接近 530 億美元，雖然日本政府尚未證實是否進場，但一名知情人士透露，日本確實採取行動支撐兌美元處於 40 多年低點的日元，美國當局也在東京時間凌晨 2 時 30 分左右進行匯率詢價。
日元周五再度強勢升值，日本銀行 (央行，BOJ) 當天如市場預期維持利率不變，但暗示為了抑制通膨與能源成本，可能進一步升息。
在日元急升之下，美債殖利率飆高，美國 10 年期公債殖利率周五上升逾 9 個基點至 4.735%，創 2023 年以來新高。
布魯金斯研究所 (Brookings Institution) 資深研究員 Robin Brooks 表示，日本為了取得美元，必須出售美國公債，再將所得美元賣出買進日元，以藉此阻止日元貶值。
他說：「在全球公債市場已經承受龐大壓力的情況下，日本債務問題正透過推高美債殖利率外溢至全球市場。」
他表示，日銀多年來透過大量買進公債壓低利率、刺激經濟，卻因此削弱日元。這迫使日本多次進場干預匯市，累計花費逾 1250 億美元，但對支撐日元效果有限。Brooks 直言：「這堪稱政府失能的最佳案例。」
美債市場本身也正承受壓力，因聯準會 (Fed) 主席 Kevin Warsh 堅持不透露政策下一步，使債券交易員只能自行判斷政策方向。
Fed 周三公布利率決議後，美國 2 年期公債殖利率走低、長天期公債殖利率走升，兩者利差擴增至 1990 年代中期以來最大。
美國 30 年期公債殖利率周五進一步攀升至 5.265%，創 2007 年金融危機爆發以來新高。
根據《日本經濟新聞》報導，日本此次干預還包括透過紐約聯準銀行進行所謂「匯率詢價」(rate check)，屬於一種「軟性干預」，即要求交易商提供匯率報價，以測試市場流動性。
凱投宏觀 (Capital Economics) 首席市場經濟學家 Jonas Goltermann 表示，這是「嶄新且相當重要的發展」，他說：「在華許令人困惑的記者會後，美元突然轉弱，再加上日本此次干預，使本輪干預性質與 4 月底的那一次短暫干預有所不同。」
Goltermann 表示，若市場再次質疑美國政策公信力，日本此次干預效果可能比前次更持久。
對美債市場而言，這是值得期待的結果，因日本仍是美國公債最大海外持有國，持有規模逾 1.4 兆美元。若日本持續干預日元並出售美債籌措資金，可能進一步推升美債殖利率，使 10 年期殖利率在年底前逼近 5%。
市場焦點因此重新回到日銀利率政策的前景上。Trading Point XM 資深市場分析師 Charalampos Pissouros 表示，若日本首相高市早苗未來任命更偏鴿派的新任日銀委員，日銀升息可能延後，政策預測也可能下修。
他認為，在市場已經面臨債務與財政赤字擴大、通膨升溫及 Fed 政策不確定性的情況下，日本帶來的新變數，正值秋季一連串利率決策、經濟數據與財政預測公布前夕，無疑讓債市雪上加霜。
paras_en: Japan's latest round of actions to stabilise the yen is having a major, potentially worrying impact on the U.S. Treasury market.

The yen surged 3.3% against the dollar on Thursday (the 30th), with foreign media speculating that the Japanese government intervened to support the currency. Based on account data and forecasts from money‑market brokers, the size of the intervention could be close to $53 billion. While the government has not confirmed whether it stepped in, a source familiar with the matter said Japan did act to bolster the yen, which has been near a 40‑year low against the dollar, and U.S. authorities also conducted a rate check in Tokyo at around 2:30 a.m. local time.
The yen rose again on Friday, and the Bank of Japan (BOJ) kept rates unchanged as markets expected, but hinted that further rate hikes could be considered to curb inflation and energy costs.
Amid the yen’s sharp appreciation, U.S. Treasury yields spiked. The 10‑year Treasury yield rose more than 9 basis points on Friday to 4.735%, a new high for 2023.
Robin Brooks, a senior researcher at the Brookings Institution, said Japan must sell U.S. Treasuries to obtain dollars, then use the proceeds to buy yen in order to stop the yen’s depreciation.
He warned that, "With the global bond market already under heavy strain, Japan’s debt issue is spilling over into the global market by pushing U.S. Treasury yields higher."

Brooks noted that the BOJ has for years bought large amounts of government bonds to keep rates low and stimulate the economy, which has weakened the yen. This has forced Japan to intervene in the FX market repeatedly, costing over $125 billion in total, with limited effect on supporting the yen. He bluntly called it "perhaps the clearest case of government dysfunction."
The Treasury market itself is under pressure because Fed Chair Kevin Warsh has refused to signal the next policy step, leaving bond traders to infer the direction on their own.
After the Fed’s rate decision on Wednesday, the 2‑year Treasury yield fell while long‑term yields rose, widening the spread to its widest since the mid‑1990s.
The 30‑year Treasury yield climbed further on Friday to 5.265%, a post‑2007‑financial‑crisis peak.
According to the Nikkei, Japan’s intervention also involved a "rate check" through the New York Fed, a form of "soft intervention" that asks dealers for price quotes to test market liquidity.

Jonas Goltermann, chief market economist at Capital Economics, called the move "a brand‑new and quite significant development," adding, "After the confusing press conference in Washington, the dollar suddenly weakened, and Japan’s intervention makes this round different from the brief one at the end of April."
Goltermann said that if markets again question the credibility of U.S. policy, Japan’s current intervention could have a more lasting impact than the previous one.

For the Treasury market, this is a development to watch, as Japan remains the largest foreign holder of U.S. Treasuries, with holdings exceeding $1.4 trillion. Continued yen‑support interventions funded by selling U.S. bonds could push Treasury yields higher, potentially bringing the 10‑year yield close to 5% before year‑end.

Market focus is therefore shifting back to the outlook for BOJ rate policy. Charalampos Pissouros, senior market analyst at Trading Point XM, said that if Prime Minister Kishida (note: likely a typo for 高市早苗) appoints a more dovish BOJ board member in the future, any BOJ rate hikes could be delayed and policy forecasts revised downwards.

He argued that, with markets already dealing with rising debt and fiscal deficits, hotter inflation and Fed policy uncertainty, Japan’s new variable adds pressure just before a series of autumn rate decisions, economic data releases and fiscal forecasts, further weighing on the bond market.

items.title: 〈紐約匯市〉美元7月跌逾1% Fed與通膨數據釋雜訊 日元連兩日強升
items.title_en: New York Forex Market: Dollar Falls Over 1% in July as Fed and Inflation Data Send Mixed Signals, Yen Rises for Second Consecutive Day
paras: 美元周五 (7/31) 下跌，7 月累計下跌逾 1%，創下 4 月以來最差單月表現。美元本周大部分跌幅出現在聯準會 (Fed) 利率決議後，外匯市場開始質疑 Fed 是否有能力有效壓制通膨，相關疑慮也反映在近期美國公債遭大舉拋售、殖利率大幅攀升。
另一方面，日元連續第二個交易日強勢升值。市場持續懷疑日本政府再度出手干預匯市，協助日元自兌美元 40 年低點反彈。這波干預預期，也掩蓋了日本央行 (BoJ) 如市場預期維持利率不變的消息。
紐約尾盤，追蹤美元兌六種主要貨幣的美元指數 (DXY) 報 99.83，7 月累計下跌 1.3%。
美國 7 月公布、反映 6 月物價表現的通膨數據，包括消費者物價指數 (CPI)、生產者物價指數(PPI) 及 Fed 偏好的通膨指標──個人消費支出物價指數(PCE)，皆低於市場預期。
不過，這波通膨降溫主要受惠於 6 月全球油價下跌。隨著中東外交局勢惡化，油價於 7 月再度走高，使市場對通膨的看法在 Fed 周三利率決議前出現明顯轉變。
雖然市場普遍預期聯邦公開市場委員會 (FOMC) 將維持利率不變，但近期油價大漲，使市場對升息的預期高於近年同期水準。最終 FOMC 決定維持聯邦基金利率不變，但有三位官員投下反對票，主張升息 1 碼。
市場原本期待 Fed 主席華許 (Kevin Warsh) 能在記者會上提出更具體的抗通膨策略或未來政策方向，但最終並未獲得明確指引。
美國公債殖利率更直接反映市場的不安情緒，7 月大幅走高，實際上已發揮類似升息的效果。
周五，三位投下反對票的官員分別發表聲明，進一步說明支持升息的理由，其中持續偏高的通膨是共同關鍵因素。Interactive Brokers 資深經濟學家 José Torres 表示，「如果 Fed 在下次會議仍不升息，固定收益市場近期的不滿情緒恐怕只會進一步惡化。」
他指出，目前「債市義警」對 Fed 感到困惑，因華許從過去被視為最鷹派的成員，如今立場已轉向委員會中間派。
Torres 表示，「這點從周三會議就能看出來。三位官員投票支持升息，但華許似乎希望繼續拖延，同時強調前任 Fed 讓通膨過長時間高於目標。」
他進一步指出，「美國公債市場正大聲告訴 Fed，不可能兩全其美。如果 9 月仍不升息，長天期公債市場將面臨更嚴重的後果。」
歐元 7 月上漲 1%
歐元兌美元小漲 0.1%，至 1.1537 美元，7 月累計上漲約 1%。
稍早公布數據顯示，歐元區 7 月整體通膨率由 6 月的 2.8% 升至 2.9%，主要受到油價反彈帶動。扣除食品與能源的核心通膨升至 2.5%。服務業通膨升至 3.3%。
再加上第二季歐元區 GDP 成長優於預期，市場更加相信歐洲央行 (ECB) 可能於 9 月升息。
目前金融市場預估，至明年初前 ECB 累計升息幅度將超過 2 碼，但經濟學家也提醒，就業市場降溫與食品通膨放緩，可能限制央行進一步大幅升息的空間。
日元連兩日走強
日元在周三大漲後，周五再度升值，美元兌日元創下 2024 年 8 月初以來最差單周表現。
《日經亞洲》報導，日本政府確實於前一天進場買進日元、賣出美元。
此外，市場人士指出，美國主管機關也曾進行匯率詢價，這通常被視為官方可能介入匯市的前兆。
日本央行稍早以 8 比 1 表決結果，將隔夜拆款利率維持在 1.0%。唯一反對票來自審議委員高田創 (Hajime Takata)，他主張在 6 月升息後，再度升息 1 碼。
日本央行同時下調核心 CPI 通膨預測，並小幅上修今年 GDP 成長預估。央行表示，政府的政策支持可望支撐經濟成長，同時有助於抑制物價壓力。
英鎊兌美元上漲 0.1%，至 1.3484 美元，7 月累計升值 1.7%。
